claim: A learned library of compressed routines plus a recognition model raises held-out solve rate and cuts search time in program-synthesis domains with strong reuse structure (text editing 3.7% to 79.6% in 10 min; LOGO and towers near 100% vs under 60% for alternatives). All numbers come from one research group (DreamCoder and its direct descendants).
agent_test: Give the agent a per-domain helper store; compare held-out solve rate with and without the store at equal total tokens (store-building tokens counted).

claim: Both compression of solutions into abstractions and a learned guide to which abstraction to try are needed; storing whole solutions without compression does worse (DreamCoder ablations, 5 runs per curve).
agent_test: Arms: no store, store of whole solved answers, store of compressed helpers; equal tokens.

claim: Compression-based library learning scales: Stitch (top-down, corpus-guided pruning) is 3-4 orders of magnitude faster and 2 orders lighter than DreamCoder compression with equal or better compression, and runs on corpora where DreamCoder times out. babble (e-graphs) independently reports better compression than DreamCoder too.
agent_test: Use a cheap symbolic step (counting repeated sub-steps across the agent's own solved traces), not an LLM call; measure compression ratio and tokens saved.

claim: Asking an LLM to do the compression step itself fails: GPT-4 produced only 19.01% valid abstractions (998 of 5250) with compression near 1.0x. One paper, best-effort prompts.
agent_test: Compare LLM-proposed helpers against mechanical dedup of repeated sub-steps at equal tokens.

claim: Unnamed library items hurt an LLM solver (-30.60 REGEX, -2.91 CLEVR, -11.11 LOGO vs plain LLM solver); LLM-written names plus docstrings recover part (+9.73, +2.27, +0.00).
agent_test: Store helpers with a name, one-line doc and worked example; ablate the doc field; equal tokens.

claim: Against a strong LLM solver with search the library adds little in two of three domains: LILO vs LLM Solver (+Search) is +0.5 REGEX, +0.3 CLEVR, +11.1 LOGO (77.07/96.76/48.95 vs 76.60/96.44/37.84; 3 seeds, LILO std 14.14 on REGEX). Most of LILO's gain over DreamCoder came from the LLM, not the library.
agent_test: Always run a strong no-library baseline with the same sampling budget.

claim: Libraries built inside the loop transfer better to plain enumeration than DreamCoder's: LILO 64.27/92.56/41.14 vs DreamCoder 41.60/91.59/30.63 (REGEX/CLEVR/LOGO), no language at test.
agent_test: Test the final helper set on fresh tasks with a plain solver and no retrieval help.

claim: Structured non-LLM search inside the loop matters most where the target needs structures language does not suggest (LOGO: 48.95 with search vs 21.02 without).
agent_test: Add a non-LLM structured-search operator for geometric or combinatorial domains; equal tokens.

claim: Library learning is not free: a LILO iteration costs about 48 CPU-hours equivalent and 0.8M-1.2M GPT tokens; dollars per iteration LILO $1.77/$1.87/$2.01 (REGEX/CLEVR/LOGO) vs DreamCoder search $1.16/$0.71/$2.07. Short-timeout domains are 2-2.5x cheaper by enumeration.
agent_test: Count library-building tokens inside the equal-token budget.

claim: Helper stores built for or with the same backbone help weaker models more than stronger ones. ReGAL from about 200 examples: CodeLlama-13B +11.5 LOGO, +26.1 Date, +8.1 TextCraft; GPT-3.5 +12.4 LOGO, +12.2 MATH but only +1.3 Date, +3.0 TextCraft, +1.8 TabMWP; some cells negative (Lemur-70B MATH 14.0 to 13.1). CRAFT (different group, toolset built by GPT-4): GPT-3.5 gains +10.4 GQA, +18.0 OK-VQA, +15.2 A-OKVQA; GPT-4 gains +4.2, +2.3, +2.5. Only two backbones in CRAFT and no study uses three sizes on one task set. The opposite pattern appears when the model writes its own memory (see K25).
agent_test: Test the helper store on a weak and a strong setting; expect the gain to shrink with model strength.

claim: In ReGAL, execution-verified helpers with retry and an easy-to-hard curriculum matter most (CodeLlama-13B dev: full LOGO 55.0, Date 77.0; no curriculum 36.3/56.6; no retry 48.3/51.9).
agent_test: Admit helpers only if they pass an execution check; order learning easy to hard; ablate each.

claim: Untrimmed libraries hurt: always-add baselines created hundreds to thousands of tools and scored below primitive-only; pruning and small libraries are needed (TroVE 16/38/8 tools vs CRAFT 282/181/525 at similar accuracy; DreamCoder and AbstractBeam also note unused items cancel gains). New: in an episodic-memory study adding every experience scored below a small fixed seed memory on all four agents (K27), and a use-count plus utility deletion rule cut memory about 4x at equal score (K28).
agent_test: Cap store size and prune by use count; compare with uncapped store at equal tokens.

claim: Direct reuse of learned tools is nearly absent in LEGO-Prover and TroVE: 1,233 of over 20,000 lemmas (6%) reached prompts and one was reused verbatim; TroVE had 3 successful reuses in 3,201 questions; blocking sharing cost 1 of 12 problems.
agent_test: Log every verbatim call of a stored item; if near zero, gains come from something else.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reported gains of LLM library methods mostly vanish at matched compute: TroVE MATH 0.24 (primitive K=15) vs 0.25 (TroVE), not significant; LEGO-Prover costs 5.84x-14.23x the baseline per attempt and the baseline matched or beat it at equal cost (4o-mini 35.9 vs 25.8 at equal attempts).
agent_test: This is our test design: every library arm gets a no-library comparator with the same total tokens spent on more samples and voting.

claim: LEGO-Prover's headline (miniF2F-valid 48.0 to 57.0, test 45.5 to 50.0, library ablation 47.1 vs 50.4 at 50 attempts) was not reproduced: 4o-mini replication 25.8 +/- 1.6 vs baseline 35.9 +/- 0.9, while gpt-4o and o3-mini LEGO-Prover led at equal attempts (29.3 vs 23.1; 27.8 vs 19.4) but not at equal compute. Check of the original paper (d22): its own text gives 52.4 valid / 45.5 test with model-written informal proofs and 55.3 / 50.0 with human-written, so the replication's '45.5% (50% with human proofs)' is accurate, not a mis-citation. Subgoal-Learning is 48.0 / 45.5.
agent_test: Treat as unverified; do not copy LEGO-Prover claims into the schema.

claim: How much benefit is stored-item reuse versus soft reuse (retrieved lemma as inspiration) is contested: LEGO-Prover authors report 24% of solved problems used retrieved skills (51% direct, 49% rewritten); the replication found no cross-task soft reuse and no survival gap between retrieved and other lemmas.
agent_test: Compare retrieval as callable, retrieval as example and random example at equal tokens.

claim: Verified executable skills beat text-only memory in agent settings: ASI 40.4% vs AWM 36.3% vs vanilla 32.7% on WebArena (claude-3.5-sonnet); AWM 35.5 vs BrowserGym 23.5 (gpt-4); Voyager's skill library is needed for tech-tree progress. Not compute-matched. Counter-evidence: an independent benchmark (Evo-Memory, Google DeepMind and UIUC) re-implemented AWM and Dynamic Cheatsheet on four embodied benchmarks and found them no better than ReAct (Claude 3.7 Sonnet average success 0.49 and 0.49-0.50 vs ReAct 0.57; Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.30 vs 0.32), while retrieving raw past experiences (ExpRAG) reached 0.63 and 0.46. Reimplementation may be weaker than the originals.
agent_test: Test verified-program vs text-note memory on repeating task families at equal tokens. Sources share authorship overlap (Wang, Neubig) for two of three.

claim: Abstractions help search only when used: AbstractBeam 53.6 vs 50.2 and 39.6 vs 36.0 on handwritten tasks (p<0.05) but 52.6 vs 53.8 and 52.4 vs 51.2 (no difference) on synthetic out-of-domain tasks.
agent_test: Report the share of stored items actually called; prune unused.

claim: Writing abstract hypotheses before code lifts ARC accuracy without any stored library: GPT-4 17% direct, 23% abstract hypotheses, 30% LLM-summarised, 33% human-selected.
agent_test: Add a hypothesis-first step; compare against more direct samples at equal tokens.

claim: DreamCoder-style compression on 36 ARC symmetry tasks gives small gains (16 solved to 22 over five rounds, five grid primitives).
agent_test: Small N; replicate on a held-out ARC subset.

claim: A library-seeded evolutionary program search reached 77.1% ARC-AGI-1 and 26.0% ARC-AGI-2 semi-private (Grok-4, about 10 calls per task, est. $2.56 per task); score-weighted softmax sampling of library programs beat greedy. Self-reported; model effect not isolated. Context (d14, d12): no ARC Prize 2024 top entry used library learning; the one peer-style LLM memory study on ARC (ArcMemo, 100 tasks, o4-mini) found a gain that faded with compute.
agent_test: Test score-weighted sampling of prior solutions vs best-first at equal tokens.

claim: People compress prospectively (for future tasks), which retrospective DreamCoder-style compression and LLM synthesis did not match when the task sequence changed (N=60: steps 3.93 vs 8.64 E1, 4.51 vs 9.56 E2).
agent_test: Let the agent build helpers for anticipated next tasks; test on drifting task sequences.

claim: Language-guided library learning helps even with no language at test: LAPS strings 33.4 to 52.2 (57.0 with mutual exclusivity); graphics best 49.55 to 98.19 but means 42.64 to 81.98; LILO's authors could not reproduce LAPS's DreamCoder baseline on LOGO (28.53 vs 42.64).
agent_test: Index helpers by natural-language description; test retrieval by description.

claim: Cross-environment reuse of LLM-written abstractions can cut repeat-task cost sharply (1,961 vs 53,376 tokens in one BabyAI level; 0 tokens in later Minihack rooms); a lifelong robot skill library beats baselines (abstract only, no numbers extracted).
agent_test: Check whether savings hold when repeats are only similar, not identical. Both are recent preprints.

claim: Direction of the model-strength effect is contested when the agent builds its own memory. Dynamic Cheatsheet: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 23.3 to 50.0, but Claude 3.5 Haiku gain is mostly from an instructions-only arm (10.0 to 26.7 with empty memory, 36.7 with memory) and GPT-4o-mini falls 16.7 to 13.3; R1 and o1 show minimal gains. Evo-Memory says smaller models benefit most (Claude 3.5 Haiku ExpRAG 0.51 vs ReAct 0.27). When a strong model writes the library and a weak one reads it, the weak one gains more (SkillWeaver GPT-4o-mini +54% vs GPT-4o +32%; ATLAS ministral-8b 5.0% to 28.3% with step-by-step hints from a frontier-model chain).
agent_test: Run the same task stream with (a) self-built store, (b) store built by a stronger model, on three model sizes; report gain over an empty-memory arm with identical instructions.

claim: Most of the gain from stored experience survives without a callable abstraction. Rule-based dedupe of action sequences matches LLM induction on WebArena (35.6 vs 35.5); text and code workflows score alike on Mind2Web; agents call workflow actions in only 18.5% of tasks; verified text in memory reaches 39.0 vs 40.1 for a callable skill (shopping); retrieving raw past experiences beats AWM and DC in Evo-Memory; CRAFT without the abstraction step keeps 31.0 of 33.4 on OK-VQA (vanilla 15.4). Counter: abstract workflows beat retrieved concrete examples on Mind2Web (+4.0 step success, gpt-3.5). No study compares callable, in-prompt example and random example on one task set.
agent_test: Three-arm test: verified helper offered as a callable, the same helper's source shown as an example, and a random verified example; plus a no-memory arm with the same instructions.

claim: Unverified accumulation hurts, and a verification gate is the most consistent single ingredient. Episodic memory with add-all scored below a small fixed seed memory on all four agents (RegAgent 55.48 vs 67.53; EHRAgent 13.05 vs 16.75; AgentDriver 32.32 vs 40.11; CIC-IoT 59.90 vs 71.50); strict filtering reached 70.95, 38.50, 51.00, 85.40. Cheap LLM judges were mixed. Dynamic Cheatsheet full-history append 26.7 vs curated 50.0 (Sonnet) and 6.7 vs 40.0 (GPT-4o). Voyager without self-verification: -73% items. ASI unverified text 32.6 vs verified text 39.0.
agent_test: Store only helpers that pass an execution check on their source task and one held-out task; compare with add-all at equal tokens.

claim: A first measured pruning rule exists for episodic memory: after a record has been retrieved at least 5 times, delete it if its mean downstream utility is below a threshold (0.3 to 0.7), plus a periodic sweep. EHRAgent strict: 38.67 at 1012 records to 42.34 at 248. AgentDriver 51.00 at 1178 to 49.97 at 323. CIC-IoT 85.40 at 904 to 85.50 at 188. With a weak GPT-4o-mini judge the rule helped EHRAgent and hurt AgentDriver. Not tested on helper functions.
agent_test: Apply the use-count plus outcome rule to a helper store; compare with no pruning and with random pruning at the same size.

claim: Reasoning-based or multi-view retrieval beats single embedding retrieval of stored items. ArcMemo: embedding retrieval of abstract concepts dropped o3-mini from 0.26 to 0.22 (15% lower; retrieved items mostly irrelevant); LLM-based selection added +4.2 at no retry but within noise at 1-2 retries. CRAFT: dropping the function-name view cost 9.0 on GQA and 6.6 on OK-VQA; SimCSE and BM25 over the same toolset scored 36.4/37.9 on GQA vs 45.4. ToolRet: all retrievers under 52% recall@10 on 43k tools, BM25 above ColBERT. No head-to-head of description vs embedding vs task signature on one agent store.
agent_test: On a store of 20 to 100 helpers compare retrieval by name+docstring text match, embedding, task-signature match and LLM selection; log hit rate and downstream score.

claim: On ARC the LLM-abstraction evidence is weak and shrinks with compute. ArcMemo (100 ARC-AGI-1 tasks, o4-mini, 3 runs, oracle@2): memory gain over baseline +4.2 at no retry (55.17 to 59.33), +0.7 at one retry, +1.8 at two (cheatsheet 71.33 beats ArcMemo-PS 70.83); sd 1.5 to 3.8. Continual memory update helped only at two retries (67.67 to 70.00). ARC Prize 2024 winners used test-time training (53.5%) and sampling of thousands of programs (about 42%); none used library learning. SOAR reached 52% by fine-tuning on relabelled attempts.
agent_test: Run a verified-helper store against verified resampling at equal tokens on a held-out ARC subset of at least 100 tasks, 3 seeds.

claim: Stitch-style symbolic compression has not been shown on an agent's own traces. The one attempt on Python (Leroy, 122 student programs of about 7 lines) pruned 3,123 macro-like, 32 invalid-parameter and about 42,000 under-20-node candidates and reached 1.04x compression (corpus grew 1.2% with the library counted). LLM-guided abstraction of agent traces exists (ATLAS) but uses automata learning, not Stitch.
agent_test: Skip symbolic compression; if tried, run on 50+ solved traces and count valid abstractions and reuse.

claim: Memory-versus-sampling comparisons published so far are not compute matched. Dynamic Cheatsheet beat 3-sample majority vote (50.0 vs 23.3 on AIME 2024) but its own footnote gives average output tokens 370 baseline, 494 instruction-only, 1035 DC-RS, 1831 DC-Cu, and the instruction-only arm already reached 36.7. With a verifier, repeated sampling scales log-linearly (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% from 1 to 250 samples) while voting plateaus near 100 samples. ArcMemo token use was similar to or above baseline.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: empty-memory instructions, verified resampling, helper store. Report tokens including store maintenance.

claim: No break-even point for library cost in tokens exists. Reported efficiency is in steps, not tokens: ReMem halves AlfWorld steps (22.6 to 11.5), ASI uses 15.3% fewer steps than vanilla; for reasoning models memory raised or matched output tokens (ArcMemo; DC-Cu about 5x baseline). Building costs: SkillWeaver 160 exploration iterations per site, LEGO-Prover about 300 US dollars per 100-attempt run, LILO about 48 CPU-hours per iteration.
agent_test: Log tokens spent building and maintaining the store; plot cumulative tokens vs tasks against the no-store arm to find the crossing point.
